description: Hi, we're SuperNova_Legacy! We're a group of enthusiastic developers and designers who love space and storytelling. Our goal for the NASA Space Apps Challenge is to give new life to the fascinating stories of the hardware & rovers left on the Moon & Mars and turn cold data into an interactive, inspirational experience for the next generation.
summary:
LEGACY — Voices Beyond Earth is an interactive storytelling experience that brings NASA’s abandoned and left-behind equipment on the Moon and Mars back into focus. Instead of presenting these objects as static artifacts, LEGACY turns their stories into an immersive digital journey. Users can explore the Moon and Mars, discover equipment connected to past missions, and follow the story of how each piece of technology was designed, used, and ultimately became part of humanity’s exploration legacy.
The project addresses this issue by transforming neglected hardware into accessible stories that connect technology, exploration and scientific discovery. It helps users understand that the equipment left on other worlds is not just discarded hardware, but may represent engineering achievements, scientific measurements and milestones in space exploration.

LEGACY combines interactive web design, visual storytelling, and NASA data to help engage a broader audience with the history and scientific value of these objects.
details:
LEGACY — Voices Beyond Earth is an interactive web-based storytelling experience designed to make the history of NASA’s left-behind and abandoned equipment on the Moon and Mars more accessible and engaging.

The project transforms space equipment from static objects into stories. Users can explore two worlds — the Moon and Mars — through an immersive interface and discover equipment associated with past space missions. Each equipment story is designed around five key questions: What is the object? Why was it sent? How was it designed to work? What scientific contribution did it support? And why does it still matter?

Our current prototype includes an interactive homepage, Moon and Mars exploration pages, rotating planetary visuals, equipment cards, navigation between experiences, and an Apollo 11 storytelling prototype. The website was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Vite. CSS is used to create the visual identity, animations, layouts, and responsive experience, while JavaScript powers the navigation and interactive elements.

The main benefit of LEGACY is accessibility. Space exploration history can often be presented through technical documents, mission archives, or isolated images. We aim to transform that information into an experience that is easier to explore and understand, especially for students, educators, and people who are curious about space but may not have a technical background.

The intended impact is to help people recognize that equipment left behind on other worlds is not simply discarded hardware. These objects can represent engineering achievements, scientific investigations, mission milestones, and important parts of humanity’s exploration history.

Creativity is at the center of the project. Instead of building a conventional information website, we designed LEGACY as a visual storytelling experience where exploration itself becomes part of learning. The Moon and Mars are treated as interactive story spaces rather than simple pages or databases.

During development, our team considered scientific accuracy, accessibility, visual clarity, technical feasibility, storytelling, and the limited time available during the hackathon. Our next development step is to integrate verified NASA resources, authentic equipment information, and scientific references into the storytelling framework so that each equipment profile can connect an engaging narrative with reliable scientific information.

Ultimately, LEGACY aims to show that a mission does not end when a spacecraft stops operating. The hardware may remain behind, but its story, scientific value, and contribution to exploration can continue to move forward.
